pac-dep-west-loch-1944.n: West Loch disaster (LST ammunition explosions), Pearl Harbor
pac-dep-west-loch-1944.what: NHHC: on 21 May 1944 LST-353, at berth T-8 in West Loch with 29 combat-loaded LSTs staging for Saipan, exploded; further explosions and fires followed into 22 May; 6 LSTs, 3 LCTs, 17 amphibious tractors and 8 howitzers lost; burning LSTs stopped about 500 ft from the ammunition depot on the south shore. Cause never established; lessons: separate gasoline and ammunition loading, enforce smoking bans, redesign LST berths.

src.t: Naval History and Heritage Command, 'Pearl Harbor Ablaze Again: The West Loch Disaster' (A. Bisno, May 2019)

pac-dep-honiara-2020.n: Honiara UXO explosion at mine-action residence (Tasahe)
pac-dep-honiara-2020.what: Norwegian People's Aid: explosion at 18:40 local time on 20 Sep 2020 in Honiara killed two NPA staff, Luke Atkinson (New Zealand; UK/Ireland dual citizen) and Trent Lee (Australia); police investigation under way; NPA's programme with the RSIPF EOD team had located and reported more than 500 explosive-ordnance items.

src.t: Norwegian People's Aid, 'Solomon Islands incident update from Norwegian People's Aid' (21 Sep 2020)

pac-mil-guam-herbicides.n: Guam: Agent Orange shipment records and herbicide use (GAO review)
pac-mil-guam-herbicides.ty: DoD / VA records · tactical herbicide (records question)
pac-mil-guam-herbicides.st: reviewed 2018; DoD location list updated Jan 2020
pac-mil-guam-herbicides.what: GAO-19-24: GAO reviewed shipping records for over 12.1 million of the 13.9 million gallons of Agent Orange procured and logbooks for 152 of 158 shipments; at least one vessel carrying Agent Orange stopped at Guam, but logbooks do not show whether cargo was loaded or unloaded; DoD's list of herbicide testing and storage locations outside Vietnam was inaccurate and incomplete; VA said the updated DoD list was released on 27 Jan 2020.

src.t: U.S. GAO, GAO-19-24 'Agent Orange: Actions Needed to Improve Accuracy and Communication of Information on Testing and Storage Locations' (15 Nov 2018)

pac-min-ranger.ty: former open-cut uranium mine, under rehabilitation · Operator: Energy Resources of Australia (ERA)
pac-min-ranger.what: DCCEEW: 8 km east of Jabiru, within the 78 km2 Ranger Project Area, surrounded by but separate from World Heritage Kakadu National Park, next to Magela Creek (East Alligator River); produced U3O8 by acid leach from 1981; mining ceased 2012 and stockpiled ore was processed until 2021; rehabilitation under way; Supervising Scientist monitoring has shown people and environment around Ranger remained protected.

pac-min-rum-jungle.ty: former uranium and copper mine; acid and metalliferous drainage · Operator: Australian Government (historic); NT Government Rum Jungle Rehabilitation team
pac-min-rum-jungle.what: NT Government: mine operated 1953-1971, producing 3,530 t uranium oxide and 20,000 t copper concentrate; legacy landforms, groundwater and surface-water contamination and AMD impacts on the East Branch of the Finniss River; Australian Government rehabilitation 1983-86 ($18.6 million) later deteriorated; joint rehabilitation since 2009 with the Kungarakan and Warai people; Stage 3 began early 2022 and is expected to span 15 years (pit backfill with lime-amended rock, new covered waste storage, river realignment).

pac-min-mount-lyell.n: Mount Lyell copper mine acid drainage (Queen and King rivers, Macquarie Harbour)
pac-min-mount-lyell.ty: historic copper-gold mine; legacy AMD, tailings and slag · Operator: Copper Mines of Tasmania (current operator, not responsible for legacy AMD)
pac-min-mount-lyell.what: EPA Tasmania: copper and gold mined for more than a century; smelter slag and tailings discharged to the rivers until smelting stopped in 1970, and tailings discharge ceased in 1994; legacy AMD from tunnels and waste-rock dumps into the Queen and King rivers is by far the most significant ongoing harm; Mt Lyell Acid Drainage Remediation Act 2003; 2002 investigations found no cost-neutral treatment option; 2013 request for proposals produced none meeting the Act's criteria.

src.t: EPA Tasmania, 'Mt Lyell Acid Drainage Remediation'

pac-min-pike-river-2010.ty: underground coal mine disaster (methane explosion) · Operator: Pike River Coal Ltd
pac-min-pike-river-2010.what: Royal Commission: at 3:45 pm on 19 Nov 2010 the mine exploded; 29 men underground died; two men in the 2.3 km stone drift escaped; three more explosions over nine days before the mine was sealed; immediate cause was ignition of a substantial volume of methane; in the last 48 days 21 reports of explosive methane levels and 27 of lesser dangerous levels; health and safety systems inadequate; the Department of Labour lacked focus and capacity to ensure compliance.

src.t: Royal Commission on the Pike River Coal Mine Tragedy, Final Report Volume 1 (30 Oct 2012)

pac-min-ok-tedi.n: Ok Tedi mine (Mount Fubilan) riverine tailings, Ok Tedi and Fly rivers
pac-min-ok-tedi.ty: open-pit copper-gold mine; riverine tailings disposal · Operator: Ok Tedi Mining Limited
pac-min-ok-tedi.what: OTML: riverine tailings discharge, approved by the Government in 1986, is the most substantial long-term environmental challenge; since 2008 sulphides are removed and the pyrite concentrate is piped over 125 km to submerged pits at Bige; dredging at Bige removes about 85% of the sand that reaches it; monitoring covers about 1,000 km down to the Gulf of Papua; in 2026 OTML submitted an ESIA for an on-land Tailings Storage Facility at Ok Birim to CEPA to largely eliminate riverine disposal.

pac-min-panguna.n: Panguna mine (Bougainville) and Kawerong-Jaba river tailings
pac-min-panguna.ty: former open-pit copper-gold mine; riverine tailings · Operator: Bougainville Copper Ltd (BCL), 'majority-owned by Rio Tinto' per Rio Tinto's 2024 release
pac-min-panguna.what: ABG (27 Apr 2023): Panguna Mine Legacy Impact Assessment field work covering impacts since mining stopped in 1989 - Loloho port, the mine, the Kawerong and Jaba rivers, Kuneka Creek, tailings-deposition areas and the delta at Empress Augusta Bay. Rio Tinto (2024): BCL operated Panguna 1972-1989, when operations were suspended by an uprising and decade-long civil war; the independent PMLIA (Tetra Tech Coffey, overseen by PNG Government, ABG, landowners, BCL, Rio Tinto and HRLC) found unstable buildings and landforms, mine-related flooding and sediment movement, and soil/water contamination from processing areas, waste rock and tailings.

src.t: Autonomous Bougainville Government, 'Field investigations to begin under Panguna Mine Legacy Impact Assessment' (27 Apr 2023)
